newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bayer says Thailand as hub for ASEAN push.
newsitem.headline: Bayer says Thailand as hub for ASEAN push.

text.p: Bayer Thai Co Ltd, a subsidiary of German chemical giant Bayer AG will use its new manufacturing site in Thailand's eastern seaboard as a hub for southeast Asian expansion, officials said on Wednesday.

The company said the site will also allow Bayer AG to open up markets in Asia in line with the company's long-term goal of seeing Asia account for 25 percent of group sales, from 17 percent at present.

"We would like to use Ma Tha Phut as chemical manufacturing site for ASEAN, but also for an export site to other Asian countries," Axel Foellmer, managing director for Bayer Thai, told Reuters in an interview. He was referring to the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
Foellmer said the company was now negotiating to buy a 50-hectare site adjacent to its existing Ma Tha Phut facilities on Thailand's eastern seaboard.
The purchase will allow Bayer options to expand beyond its existing 25-hectare site.

Expansion options under consideration include the possible building of a Bisphenol A plant which would bring total site output of this raw material for polycarbonate production to 80,000 tonnes per year.
Expansion of polycarbonate production at the existing site requires Board of Investment approva, which is pending and expected during the first quarter of this year, Foellmer said.
The first phase of the expansion should see Bayer producing 40,000 tonnes of polycarbonate by 1999.
Second phase expansion, on stream by 2001-2002, should double output.
In addition, first phase facilities are set to produce around 75,000 tonnes of styrene-based ABS and SAN per year.
The new facilities, in which Bayer is going to invest approximately $400 million, represent Bayer's single largest investment in Asia, Foellmer said.
Approximately 70 percent of the total output will be for export and the remainder for the Thai market, Foellmer said.
Thailand currently accounts for around 40 percent of Bayer's sales within the ASEAN region which are projected to total $330 million in 1997.
Bayer already has two plants near Bangkok which make animal health, drug and agrochemical products.
Foellmer said Bayer was also likely to have discussions to develop its polyurethane business, in which the company sees substantial growth potential in the region.
Bayer currently sells around 360 million baht ($14.4 million) of polyurethane in Thailand each year. ($1=25 baht)
